title: Find an antiderivative
text: Let $$u=x$$ and $$dv=e^{\left(-2x\right)} dx$$. An antiderivative is $$-\left(\frac{1}{2}\right) x e^{\left(-2x\right)}-\frac{1}{4} e^{\left(-2x\right)}$$.

title: Evaluate
text: At $$x=1$$ the antiderivative is $$\frac{-3}{4e^2}$$. At $$x=0$$ it is $$\frac{-1}{4}$$. Subtract to get $$\frac{1}{4}-\frac{3}{4e^2}$$.
